title: Chapter 199: Fang Hwa Apartments
html:
“Even the police can’t find information on them?” Chen Ge was shocked. “Which three patients are missing? Perhaps I can provide more clues.”

“You remember details from four or five years ago?” Chen Ge had surprised Captain Yan repeatedly. Given his contribution to the Ping An Apartments case, the captain was willing to share limited information. “They occupied Rooms 7, 9, and 10 in the Third Sick Hall.”

Chen Ge committed the numbers to memory and compared them with Doctor Gao’s information. Patient No. 7 had Cotard’s syndrome, also called walking-corpse syndrome. He believed himself dead and insisted that his organs had already decayed.

Hospital records listed him as deceased, but Doctor Gao had merely read that entry; no one he knew had seen the body. The record could have been fabricated.

Patient No. 9 was Wu Fei, whom Men Nan’s original personality had warned him about. Patient No. 10 was the man both doctors and patients called the Devil. Almost no information existed about him, but the former director must have known more; as head of the institution, he controlled its records.

Unfortunately, Zhang Ya had torn the director apart, leaving only his head behind the door. Extracting information from him would be difficult. Chen Ge’s thoughts shifted. After Xu Tong and the patient with Phantom Limb Syndrome died, the mission’s completion rate rose by five percent. That suggested a path forward. Will capturing or killing the other escaped patients continue raising the completion rate?

It was entirely possible. The patients had received new life from the door, which had marked them. Technically, they had become part of the Third Sick Hall.

After Chen Ge remained silent for some time, Captain Yan continued. “We tried to interview former doctors and nurses about those three patients, but uncovered something terrible.”

“What is it?”

“Every doctor familiar with them died mysteriously—some in accidents, others by apparent suicide.” Captain Yan paused, considering whether to continue.

“Captain Yan, I promise to not leak anything you tell me.”

“I’m not worried about a leak. I don’t want to frighten you.” His tone shifted. “The strangest victim was a female doctor who moved away from Jiujiang with her boyfriend but still couldn’t escape. The deaths occurred in different places and appeared unrelated, with no obvious timing pattern, so no one connected them. Once the Third Sick Hall link emerged, we reviewed the cases and found new patterns. Excluding genuine accidents, roughly ninety percent were carefully planned murders.”

Captain Yan was trying to warn Chen Ge that his situation was very dangerous.

“They certainly are bold.” With a dry laugh, Chen Ge headed toward the exit. He wanted to leave and return to New Century Park as quickly as possible.

“They’re fanatics. They don’t think like ordinary people and will stop at nothing. Worst of all, they genuinely believe they’ve done no wrong. That makes them extremely difficult to confront.” Captain Yan sounded weary. “Be careful. If you discover anything, contact me immediately.”

“Okay.” Before Captain Yan hung up, Chen Ge said, “Captain Yan, other than these three patients, you also have the information on the other patients, right? Can I take a look at them? After all, I’m the only one who has interacted with them before.”

“I’m warning you, don’t do anything stupid.”

“You misunderstand. I’m merely curious. If you know where some patients are, why not arrest and question them now?” His life was at stake, so Chen Ge could never be too cautious. “Are you afraid of alerting the others? Do you plan to capture them simultaneously?”

“If only it were that simple…” Captain Yan offered no details, but the investigation had clearly encountered trouble. “This information isn’t public, but since you’re one of their victims, I’ll select several files you’re permitted to see and send them over.”

After a few final words, Captain Yan ended the call and sent the files. Each patient had an assigned number, and the police had compiled the available information into individual dossiers.

“Room 1, Wang Shenglong…” His dossier was the most detailed, listing every recent treatment, each address from the past five years, and the people he had contacted. The police knew virtually everything about him.

The second dossier concerned a woman whose face looked almost unnaturally perfect, yet somehow seemed not to belong to her. Chen Ge remembered Doctor Gao describing her Dorian Gray syndrome: an extreme fear of aging that drove her through repeated cosmetic surgery and heavy makeup. Police records showed that she vanished six months earlier after last being seen at Fang Hwa Apartments.

The location made Chen Ge’s heart jolt. Too many threads converged on the same place for coincidence. He hurried through the remaining scenes toward the exit.

Light appeared ahead. Several yards from the exit, he encountered six or seven people huddled together, creeping forward with grim expressions.

“What are you guys doing?” Chen Ge walked toward them with the tape recorder.

“Wait!” the proprietor yelled at Chen Ge through the loudspeaker. “Are… are you alright?”

“Why wouldn’t I be? Do you think I’m possessed?” Chen Ge shrugged and walked past the proprietor and his staff. “Your Haunted House is safe now. But remember: money earned by exploiting the dead may carry a curse.”

The light outside was almost blinding. Every visitor turned toward Chen Ge, the first man they had ever seen enter a Haunted House and frighten all its “ghosts” into fleeing. He had accomplished what no ordinary guest could.
